event.centerRule: Genesis 22:1–19 remains the sole narrated witness and complete Event boundary. Antecedents, aftermath, later location, and later memories remain distinct sources. Later interpretation may be compared but never used to fill Genesis’s silence about Isaac.

characterAnchors.label: Abraham
characterAnchors.note: Receives the command, prepares the journey, answers Isaac, builds the altar, is halted, offers the ram, and hears the oath.

characterAnchors.label: Isaac
characterAnchors.note: Is named as the loved son, carries the wood, asks about the lamb, is bound and spared, and later becomes the subject of remembered interpretations.

characterAnchors.label: God
characterAnchors.note: Frames the test, issues the opening command, and is named in Abraham’s words about provision.

characterAnchors.label: The LORD’s angel
characterAnchors.note: Calls from heaven, halts harm to Isaac, names the test’s result, and delivers the oath.

characterAnchors.label: Sarah
characterAnchors.note: Receives the promise of Isaac, bears him, and is remembered in the family aftermath.

characterAnchors.label: Ishmael
characterAnchors.note: Remains Abraham’s son and is preserved in the neighboring family account before Genesis calls Isaac the only son in the test.

event.throughline: Promise and family separation lead to a test in which Abraham takes Isaac toward Moriah. Isaac asks about the offering, Abraham speaks of provision, the altar action is halted, a ram is offered instead, and a renewed oath follows. Later sources remember the Event for different arguments.

topic.orientation: Enter Genesis 22:1–19 as one Event told in nine reading movements. Earlier family Scenes set the promise and two sons in view. Later sources remember the Event through testing, compassion, faith, works, and resurrection reasoning.
